title: priority-gardener: adaptive backpressure to arrest burst-sputter latency across deployments
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Multiple customers reported sudden TTFT spikes and tokens/sec collapse after a kernel selector tweak rolled last week. Impact spanned Hosted API, several Dedicated clusters, and a Private customer on our 1.24 branch. Root pattern shows short (10s–2m) ‘burst-sputter’ episodes: initial priming tokens stream fine, then emission rate drops and first-token latency climbs while queues back up in the fastpath. This ticket coordinates an emergency production hotfix (adaptive backpressure controller, internal codename 'priority-gardener'), short-term mitigations, customer comms, and the follow-up postmortem + longer-term telemetry/guardrails.
symptoms_observed: TTFT spike (median -> p95 from 40ms -> 420ms) during short fanout bursts
tokens/sec drop by 60% for affected model variants
occurs across hosted/dedicated/private — correlation with small-session priming and kv-prefetch enabled
stack traces show dispatcher fastpath queue growth and persistent kernel handoff latency
affected_customers: Ledgerly (dedicated, financial summarization), private pilot - NovaGov (on-prem)
investigation_summary: Traces and heap/queue telemetry from 03-10 morning show priority inversion: small priming requests with KV-prefetch reserve fastpath slots and trigger int8-optimized kernels that later block on a rare kernel preemption path. The scheduler's admission logic failed to age low-priority inflight priming, leaving the fastpath saturated and starving ongoing token emission. Reproduced in staging by replaying customer traffic patterns with fanout=4 and priming_length=32. Profiling indicates avg dispatch->emit latency increases following a kernel-selection fallback within 3s of session start.
short_term_mitigation_deployed: 03-11 02:00 UTC: enabled conservative kernel fallback on affected pools (rollback of kernel selection heuristic) - rollback ID: rs-20260311-kf-3
03-11 03:30 UTC: throttled kv-prefetch per-session (config kv_prefetch.max_concurrent -> 2) in Hosted canaries
03-12 09:00 UTC: pushed priority-gardener v0.1 to two Dedicated clusters as a canary (adaptive backpressure controller that enforces token-emission floor and ages priming reservations)
03-12 11:45 UTC: emergency customer bridge and interim status notes to OrbitalHealth and Ledgerly with mitigation steps and ETA for full rollout
hotfix_notes: priority-gardener v0.1 implements a per-workload token-emission monitor and a low-latency shedder: when observed tokens/sec falls below configured threshold for >2s, gardener signals scheduler to deprioritize priming reservations and temporarily broaden kernel selection tolerance. Hotfix intentionally conservative to avoid correctness regressions. Telemetry added to track shedder activations and end-to-end TTFT impact.
pending_actions: Complete full rollout of priority-gardener to remaining Dedicated pools (target 03-14) after metric stability window
Staged rollout to hosted API regions with 2-hour canaries and automatic rollback on p95 TTFT > 300ms
Confirm Private on-prem upgrade path for NovaGov and provide patch instructions + support window
Add automated regression test that replays priming-heavy fanout in CI harness and fails if tokens/sec drops >40%
postmortem_outline: Root cause: scheduler admission + kernel-selection interplay exposed by priming-heavy short sessions. Missing guardrail: no token-emission floor enforced and no aging for priming reservations. Follow-ups: formalize emitter-level SLO, implement shedder as permanent controller, improve kernel preemption telemetry, and add canary tests for kernel selector changes.
